topics.topic: Redefining Growth: India's Revised GDP Estimates and the New Measurement Framework
topics.why_in_news: Government released revised GDP estimates and introduced updated measurement framework to improve accuracy, sectoral representation and economic data reliability.
prelims_quick_notes: GDP measures total value of goods and services produced.
Revision aimed at improving accuracy of national income estimation.
New framework incorporates updated databases and methodologies.
Base-year revisions important for reflecting structural economic changes.
Digital economy and services sector gaining greater representation.
National accounts prepared by National Statistical Office (NSO).
GDP estimates influence fiscal and monetary policymaking.
Formalisation and data integration improving statistical coverage.
important_facts: NSO functions under Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
GDP can be measured by production, income and expenditure methods.
Real GDP adjusted for inflation while nominal GDP is not.
Base year revision improves comparability and relevance.
GVA measures value addition by producers.
GDP excludes many unpaid household activities.
key_highlights: Updated framework improved sectoral representation.
Use of digital and administrative databases increased.
Better capture of emerging economic activities emphasised.
Focus on improving reliability and international comparability.
Formal sector data integration strengthened estimation process.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Statistics and Economic Planning.
Useful for national income accounting and growth-measurement topics.
Can be linked with fiscal policy and development indicators.
prelims_traps: GDP and GVA are related but different indicators.
Base-year revision does not automatically imply higher growth.
NSO prepares India’s national income estimates.

topics.topic: Union Budget 2026–27: Rural Transformation through Decentralization
topics.why_in_news: Union Budget 2026–27 emphasised rural transformation through decentralised governance, localised development planning and strengthening grassroots institutions.
prelims_quick_notes: Decentralisation promotes local-level governance and participation.
Rural transformation linked with Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).
Budget focused on inclusive and region-specific rural development.
Gram Panchayats play major role in local implementation.
Fiscal devolution strengthens local governance capacity.
Rural infrastructure and livelihood diversification prioritised.
Digital governance increasingly integrated into rural administration.
Decentralised planning improves accountability and efficiency.
important_facts: 73rd Constitutional Amendment institutionalised Panchayati Raj.
Eleventh Schedule contains subjects related to Panchayats.
Finance Commissions recommend grants to local bodies.
Gram Sabha acts as foundation of local democracy.
Rural development linked with agriculture and non-farm employment.
Decentralisation supports participatory governance.
key_highlights: Budget stressed grassroots-driven rural development.
Focus on local infrastructure and service delivery.
Digital tools and DBT integration expanded.
Emphasis on rural entrepreneurship and livelihoods.
Strengthening of local institutions highlighted.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Governance and Rural Development.
Useful for decentralisation and inclusive growth topics.
Can be linked with Panchayati Raj and fiscal federalism.
prelims_traps: 73rd Amendment relates to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Gram Sabha differs from Gram Panchayat.
Decentralisation includes administrative, fiscal and political dimensions.

topics.topic: Ease of Doing Business: India’s Ongoing Regulatory Transformation
topics.why_in_news: Government highlighted ongoing regulatory reforms aimed at improving Ease of Doing Business through digitisation, decriminalisation and streamlined compliance mechanisms.
prelims_quick_notes: Ease of Doing Business focuses on reducing regulatory burden.
Regulatory reforms aim to improve investment climate.
Digitisation simplifies approvals and compliance processes.
Decriminalisation of minor offences encourages business confidence.
Single-window systems improve administrative efficiency.
MSMEs benefit from simplified compliance procedures.
Reforms linked with Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Business environment influences investment and employment generation.
important_facts: Jan Vishwas reforms focus on decriminalisation of minor offences.
DPIIT plays key role in investment and industrial facilitation.
Digital governance reduces transaction costs.
MSMEs form major share of employment generation.
Regulatory simplification linked with competitiveness improvement.
India improved significantly in World Bank Ease of Doing Business rankings before its discontinuation.
key_highlights: Compliance reduction measures expanded.
Digital approval systems strengthened.
Focus on reducing legal and procedural delays.
Reforms aimed at improving investor confidence.
Technology-driven governance emphasised.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Governance and Industrial Development.
Useful for investment climate and regulatory reforms topics.
Can be linked with MSMEs, startups and economic growth.
prelims_traps: Ease of Doing Business differs from Ease of Living.
Digital governance important for compliance simplification.
MSMEs are major beneficiaries of regulatory reforms.

topics.why_in_news: Union Budget 2026–27 presented comprehensive fiscal roadmap focusing on growth, infrastructure, welfare, green transition and employment generation.
prelims_quick_notes: Union Budget is annual financial statement under Article 112.
Budget includes estimates of receipts and expenditure.
Fiscal policy used for growth, welfare and macroeconomic stability.
Capital expenditure emphasised for infrastructure creation.
Focus on employment, manufacturing and digital economy.
Green growth and energy transition prioritised.
Fiscal consolidation balanced with development spending.
Budget reflects government’s economic priorities and reforms.
important_facts: Article 112 deals with Annual Financial Statement.
Finance Bill contains taxation proposals.
Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha.
Fiscal deficit represents excess of expenditure over revenue excluding borrowings.
Capital expenditure creates long-term productive assets.
Revenue expenditure relates to routine administrative spending.
key_highlights: Infrastructure and capital expenditure increased.
Support for MSMEs and manufacturing strengthened.
Digital and AI-driven economy promoted.
Green energy and climate initiatives expanded.
Focus on inclusive growth and employment generation.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Fiscal Policy and Governance.
Useful for budgeting process and macroeconomic management topics.
Can be linked with inclusive growth and infrastructure development.
prelims_traps: Money Bills can originate only in Lok Sabha.
Capital expenditure differs from revenue expenditure.
Fiscal deficit excludes borrowings from receipts.
Article 112 relates to Annual Financial Statement.
